status_summary: Army active-component end strength authorized in law rose from 442,300 in FY2025 to 454,000 for 2026-09-30 in the FY2026 NDAA (P.L. 119-60, enacted 2025-12-18), an increase of 11,700, and CRS says the FY2027 request would add 18,300 to Total Army end strength, against the Mandate's 50,000 force structure increase. Under the Army Transformation Initiative (a Secretary of Defense memo of 2025-04-30 and an Army letter of 2025-05-01) the Army was directed to cancel procurement of the AH-64D and of excess HMMWV, JLTV and Gray Eagle systems, and Army Futures Command and TRADOC were merged on 2025-10-01. Defense News reported on 2026-07-14, citing a DOD Inspector General evaluation, that 155mm output was about 36,000 rounds a month as of March 2026, up from about 14,000, against a goal of 100,000 a month by October 2025. Whether the six listed modernization priorities are being accelerated was not established.

timeline.event: Secretary of Defense issues the Army Transformation and Acquisition Reform memo; the Army's letter to the force of 2025-05-01 directs cancelling procurement of the AH-64D and of excess HMMWV, JLTV and Gray Eagle systems and trimming headquarters.
Army Futures Command and TRADOC are merged into the Army Transformation and Training Command (T2COM).
FY2026 NDAA signed; Army active-component end strength set at 454,000, up from 442,300 in FY2025.
Defense News reports 155mm output of about 36,000 rounds a month as of March 2026 against a 100,000 goal, with metal parts production the limiting factor.

title: Grow Army force structure by 50,000, speed modernization and boost munitions output
uncertainties: The text of Sec. 401 of P.L. 119-60 could not be read: the govinfo HTML and PDF truncate before Title IV and Congress.gov refuses automated fetches, so the end strength figures rest on CRS Insight IN12651, which does not cite the section. The 50,000 comparison uses authorized active-component end strength, not actual strength or total force structure; the FY2027 figure of 18,300 is for Total Army end strength. CRS R48606 (updated 2026-05-21) does not mention the six priorities or munitions production, and describes the cancellations as directed actions without confirming that each program has ended. The Defense News figures rely on a DOD IG report not read directly, and the timing of the earlier 14,000 rate is not given. Other munitions were not examined.
